principles.statement: Use job control deliberately for interactive jobs, knowing how process groups, backgrounding, suspension, fg/bg/jobs/disown, and terminal signals affect job lifetime and input.
applies_when: When controlling interactive or long-running shell work.
Managing commands launched from an interactive terminal.

principles.statement: Use SSH-family tools for encrypted remote login and file transfer, with explicit credentials, protected keys, host-key awareness, ports, agents, terminal options, and clean session closure.
applies_when: When connecting to remote machines.
When copying files to or from an SSH-accessible machine.
When connecting to or transferring files with remote machines.
Authenticating or transferring data across a network.

principles.statement: Inspect files and directories before modifying them, and use interactive or attribute-preserving options when overwrites, copies, moves, or recursive deletion carry risk.
applies_when: When setting up sample data or handling unfamiliar files.
When managing files and folders from the shell.
When performing basic file operations.

principles.statement: Before deleting or executing from find results, verify the result set with printing or prompts and choose safer per-file or batched execution modes deliberately.
applies_when: When find will delete files or execute commands on matches.
Using find -delete, -exec, -ok, or xargs.

principles.statement: Use Linux directory conventions as diagnostic hints, but take a read-only system-tour approach and verify actual contents and permissions before editing system files.
applies_when: When reasoning about system paths, pseudo-filesystems, ownership, or permissions.
Learning or auditing an unfamiliar Linux system.

principles.statement: Before storage operations, name the storage layer precisely and map block devices, partitions, filesystems, mount points, and directories with df or lsblk.
applies_when: When diagnosing or modifying storage.
Preparing removable or disk-like storage.

principles.statement: Use backup and sync tools with exact source/destination semantics, dry runs, and transport choices, especially rsync for repeated attribute-preserving synchronization.
applies_when: When copying, mirroring, synchronizing, or burning backup data.
Synchronizing local or remote file trees.

principles.statement: Favor symbolic links for routine references, understand which operations affect the link versus the target, and prefer relative targets for movable trees.
applies_when: When creating or diagnosing links.
Creating or maintaining links between pathnames.

principles.statement: Choose the line-editing mode with 'editing-mode' in the inputrc or 'set -o emacs'/'set -o vi'; in vi mode a new line starts in insert mode and ESC enters command mode (k/j move through history).
applies_when: Editing text in vi or vim.

principles.statement: Signal processes with the least force that can work, escalating from normal termination to named signals, timeouts, and KILL only after ordinary termination fails.
applies_when: When stopping processes or bounding runtime.
Stopping, resuming, or controlling processes.

principles.statement: Handle archives by first choosing the archive family and action, naming the archive explicitly, selecting compression flags by format, and controlling extraction destination.
applies_when: When packaging, listing, or extracting archived/compressed files.
Sharing archives with Windows users or ZIP-only tools.

principles.statement: Learn a terminal editor for remote and shell-only editing, and store its reusable configuration in dotfiles.
applies_when: When editing on remote servers, containers, or terminals without desktop editors.
Editing files over terminals, recovery shells, or non-GUI systems.

principles.statement: Verify the current directory, listings, hidden files, and path forms before running location-dependent commands; use absolute paths or home-directory forms intentionally.
applies_when: When navigating or operating on files from the shell.
When commands operate on relative or user-home paths.

principles.statement: Treat rm and shell deletion as permanent; preview wildcard targets and prefer interactive or nonrecursive removal unless recursive deletion is clearly intended.
applies_when: When removing files or directories.
Deleting files, especially with wildcards or recursive options.

principles.statement: Use compression tools with awareness of file replacement, stdout modes, integrity testing, compression levels, viewing helpers, speed, and recovery behavior.
applies_when: When compressed content should feed another command or originals must remain.
Compressing or viewing compressed files.

principles.statement: Treat raw device copying with dd as high risk, verifying input and output devices and media type before running as root because mistakes can destroy data.
applies_when: When copying disks, partitions, or raw device data.
Using dd, ISO images, or optical media writing tools.

principles.statement: Access clipboards only through mechanisms supported by the active graphical or terminal environment, and choose the correct X selection for the paste target.
applies_when: When copying and pasting between shell and other applications.
When moving data between shell and clipboard.

principles.statement: Compare and verify files with tools and checksum strength that match the question, using quiet modes in scripts and saved strong checksums for later integrity checks.
applies_when: When checking differences or integrity.
When comparisons need to drive automation.
Using downloaded disk, ISO, or binary images.

principles.statement: Design prompts with safe PS syntax, bracketing non-printing terminal sequences and accounting for any later prompt expansion of dynamic fields.
applies_when: When customizing command prompts.

principles.statement: Inspect host, interface, address, route, DHCP, and gateway facts with current tools, preferring iproute2 output over legacy interface tools.
applies_when: When diagnosing local host or network-interface state.
Diagnosing local network configuration.

principles.statement: Mount and unmount filesystems through fstab-aware commands when possible, and unmount writable removable media before removal while respecting busy-filesystem refusals.
applies_when: When accessing or removing mounted filesystems.
Removing, repairing, or detaching storage.

principles.statement: Use terminal-native editing, history, and clipboard conventions to edit commands safely instead of relying on ordinary GUI shortcuts.
applies_when: When a pending shell command needs substantial edits.
Editing or reusing commands in a terminal emulator or virtual console.

principles.statement: Create, truncate, or timestamp files intentionally; use shell redirection for simple empty-file creation or truncation when touch-specific timestamp behavior is not required.
applies_when: The goal is only to create or empty a file.
When creating placeholders or changing timestamps.

principles.statement: Prefer repository-backed package management for ordinary software maintenance, using high-level tools for dependency-aware operations and low-level package-file installation only cautiously.
applies_when: Installing or maintaining Linux software.
Managing packages from distribution repositories.
Installing a downloaded package file directly.

principles.statement: Master tmux panes, windows, sessions, attach, detach, naming, and cleanup before adding advanced customizations such as Vim-style keys, styling, plugins, or advanced pane operations.
applies_when: When adopting tmux as a daily tool.
When basic tmux use exposes real limitations.

principles.statement: Navigate by maintaining awareness of the current directory and choosing clear absolute, relative, home, or previous-directory path forms.
applies_when: Working with files or directories from the shell.

principles.statement: Manage user accounts, shells, passwords, locks, groups, and IDs conservatively as persistent security state affecting login access and file ownership.
applies_when: When creating, modifying, or removing local user accounts.
When administering users and groups.

principles.statement: Use tar modes and path handling deliberately for archive creation, extraction, ownership, selective restore, incremental archives, standard streams, compression, file-list input, and SSH pipelines.
applies_when: Creating, extracting, restoring, or transporting tar archives.
Archiving selected files or copying trees between systems.

principles.statement: Diagnose processes by understanding parent-child relationships, ownership, PID identity, daemon role, and snapshot versus live views.
applies_when: Investigating running programs or system slowdown.

principles.statement: Use tmux for persistent, organized, remote-friendly terminal sessions, including SSH sessions that should resume after disconnects.
applies_when: When managing multiple shell tasks or remote work.
When remote shell sessions should be durable.

principles.statement: Understand mounting through fstab, labels or UUIDs, mount points, mount listings, and filesystem types before manually attaching storage.
applies_when: Inspecting or manually mounting storage devices.

principles.statement: For copy, move, and remove operations, choose options that match overwrite, recursion, update, and confirmation requirements before executing.
applies_when: Manipulating files or directories with mkdir, cp, mv, or rm.

principles.statement: Use lp and a2ps layout controls with upstream pagination alignment when print orientation, density, scaling, page ranges, or pretty PostScript output matter.
applies_when: Formatting and submitting print jobs.

principles.statement: Understand Linux printing as a CUPS and Ghostscript workflow with queues, conversion, page description, and rasterization.
applies_when: Printing or troubleshooting printer workflows from the command line.
